name: AI for Developers

sources.title: Homepage — live curated directory of AI agents, SDKs, coding copilots, and dev-first tools
Contribute — suggest a tool via GitHub issue at tokyo-dal/awesome-ai-coding-tools, or email for creator features/collaboration

requirements: Dev-first AI tools only: agents, SDKs, coding copilots, IDE assistants, app builders, frameworks, models
Suggestions go through a GitHub issue on the awesome-ai-coding-tools repo, or corrections the same way
Creators seeking a feature can email the editors (address is Cloudflare-obfuscated on /page/contribute)
Editorial curation — no self-serve instant listing
preparation: Tool name, URL, and a one-line pitch of why it belongs
Category fit (IDE Assistants, App Builders, Coding Agents, Frameworks, Models, Open Source)
GitHub account to open the suggestion issue
If the creator: an email pitch for featuring/collaboration
workflow: Check the tool isn't already listed (search /tool/<slug> pages or category lists)
Open an issue at github.com/tokyo-dal/awesome-ai-coding-tools suggesting the tool
Or email the contact address (deobfuscate on /page/contribute) as the product's creator requesting a feature
Editors add accepted tools to /tool/<slug> pages and category lists
watchFor: No self-serve submission form — it's suggestion-then-editorial-review
The GitHub suggestion route is an 'awesome list' style repo, not a form with fields — write a concise, factual pitch
Separate /advertise page exists for paid placement
Free-tools and open-source filters exist on the listing — being genuinely dev-focused matters more than polish
countsAsLive: The tool appears on a /tool/<slug> page on aifordevelopers.org and in its category's 'See all' list
unknowns: Acceptance criteria and turnaround for GitHub suggestions
Whether being 'featured' via email implies paid placement or editorial choice
Exact contact email (Cloudflare-protected on the page)
